subject: APAC edge onramp and US/EU capacity redistribution — tradeoff matrix

Subject: APAC edge onramp — preliminary traffic profile and ask

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a concrete ask: NimbusAI is aiming to roll out a low-latency + privacy-sensitive feature in Singapore and Tokyo by May 15. Expected steady-state is ~18k requests/day with 95th percentile latency target <150ms; peak can hit up to 4x steady during marketing bursts.

Given the latency targets and regulatory needs, we're asking Redwood to:
- Provision a small APAC edge dedicated pool for inference (initially 6 x A100-equivalent GPU-days persistent, with 12 GPU-days burstable)
- Guarantee route isolation for our traffic and a pathway to scale to 24 persistent GPUs within 90 days if the pilot looks good

I've attached our traffic projection sheet and a short note on data residency constraints. Can you share a tradeoff matrix that maps: cold start latency, effective cost/TU, and ops complexity across options (APAC edge pool vs EU fallback vs US with CDN)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up.

— Amrita Rao
Head of Product, NimbusAI
amrita@nimbus.ai

Subject: RE: APAC edge onramp — preliminary traffic profile and ask

All,

I've modeled three options and attached the tradeoff matrix PDF:
A) APAC edge dedicated pool (Singapore + Tokyo single-region nodes) — 6 persistent GPUs (p4d/A100-equivalent), burst to 18 for launch. Pros: lowest client latency, compliance-friendly. Cons: ~25-35% infra cost premium; additional ops for peering and local monitoring.
B) EU fallback with regional CDN + smart routing — keep core inference in EU, use caching at CDN and prefix-KV caching to hit latency target. Pros: Faster to deploy; lower infra cost. Cons: ~20-50ms added median latency compared to edge, potential regulatory issues depending on dataset residency.
C) US primary with edge-accelerated CDN — cheapest but likely misses the 95th<150ms SLA during peaks for Tokyo/Singapore.

Sizing assumptions (see sheet): each p4d-equivalent GPU supports ~180 qps for our model at target latency with batching disabled; pilot steady-state 18k req/day -> average qps ~0.2, peak qps ~0.8; conservative headroom -> 6 GPUs persistent with 2x batching headroom for bursts.

Estimated monthly cost delta (APAC vs EU): +32% for persistent + networking. Time-to-live for a full APAC onramp (infrastructure + certs + peering): ~4–6 weeks if we prioritize.

Recommendation: Start with Option A at 6 persistent / 12 burstable, include automatic fallback to EU on overload, and commit to a 60-day review to scale to 24 persistent if usage metrics warrant.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Quick operational notes (TL;DR):
- Network: We'll need a customer VPC peering or private link in SG/TK. Lead time varies by provider (2–3 weeks if we have existing accounts, 4–6 otherwise).
- Monitoring/Alerts: Add a regional latency SLO and auto-failover playbook. Ops can own a canary route for the first 72 hours post-launch, then hand off to Nimbus.
- SLA: We can offer a pilot SLA with an objective latency target (non-credit) and a defined escalation path. Production SLA requires 90-day capacity commit for 24 GPUs.

Amrita — for procurement, we'll need: contact for network team, preferred cloud partners for APAC (GCP Singapore, AWS ap-southeast-1, OCI is OK), and a signed pilot MOU covering the 60-day review and scaling clause.

Ben Carter
Director, Regional Operations, Redwood Inference
